w:r.w:t: Version 2.0 | Based on Full Requirements Analysis

This document defines the complete implementation plan for the Internal Audit Management System (IAMS). It is based on a thorough analysis of all stated requirements and covers all modules including Registration & Authentication, Audit Engagements, Audit Work Program (AWP), Management of Verification (MOVs), Dashboards, and supplementary modules.
The system must enforce strict role-based access. The following roles are defined:
Create + New Audit Engagement; Approve AWP; Sign Off
Co-equal with Director for engagement creation
Create + New Audit Engagement; Approve AWP; Sign Off
Manage engagement team; Add Assistant Leader; Review & Sign Off AWP
Designated inside an engagement by TL
Review & Sign Off AWP; NOT a separate login account
Access assigned engagement tools; Upload MOVs; No + New Engagement button
View relevant engagement info; Respond to MOV dropdowns

The Assistant Team Leader (ATL) is NOT a standalone login account. It is a designation assigned by the Team Leader from within the Audit Engagement after creation. The ATL shares the same authentication credentials as a regular Auditor account but is tagged as ATL within a specific engagement.
The registration form must support the following:
Email Address — must accept both .gov.ph government emails and Gmail addresses
Role selection dropdown: Director, Division Chief, Team Leader, Auditor, Auditee
Upon submission, system sends a confirmation link to the registered email
Account is inactive until email is verified
If email ends in .gov.ph — recognized as government email; confirmation sent to that address
If email is a Gmail address — standard Gmail OAuth-style confirmation flow
Both types must go through email verification before account activation
Forgot Password — user enters registered email; system sends a reset link
Reset Password — user clicks link in email and enters a new password
Change Password — available from the user profile/settings page while logged in
System redirects user to their role-specific dashboard after login
Gov mail users can also use their email to log in normally (not OAuth dependency)
The Dashboard is the central hub of the system. It must display real-time data aggregated from all modules. Each role sees a version of the dashboard relevant to their permissions.
AWP Status Panel — shows open AWPs and their current approval stage
Audit Engagements Panel — list of active and past engagements
MOV Progress Panel — visual progress tracker for MOVs per engagement
Notifications Panel — alerts for responsible personnel when AWP is opened or updated
Generated Tools Panel — links to all tools generated under each engagement
Only Directors and Division Chiefs can create a new audit engagement. The + New Audit Engagement button must be hidden or disabled for all other roles.
The + New Audit Engagement form must include:
Type of Audit — dropdown with options:
(+ Add option to insert additional types if needed)
After the engagement is created, the assigned Team Leader can:
Add an Assistant Team Leader (ATL) — this is a dropdown/search field to select from registered Auditor accounts; the selected person is tagged as ATL for this engagement only
Add Auditors to the engagement team
Access all audit tools for this engagement
Auditors and Auditees are enrolled into a specific engagement. Once enrolled, the engagement appears on their dashboard and they receive notifications related to it.
The AWP must be open and visible to ALL users enrolled in the engagement. Any update or opening of an AWP must trigger a notification to all responsible personnel.
The AWP table must support adding dynamic rows via an Add Row (+) button at the bottom of each section. This applies to all file/table sections within the AWP.
The AWP follows a structured approval chain:
Initial preparation and drafting of AWP
Review and sign-off at review level
Each stage (Reviewed by, Approved by) must have a Sign Off button. Rules:
Clicking Sign Off records: user's name, role, and exact date/time
Multiple people can sign off on the same document at different times — all are recorded
The most recent sign-off is visible on the main AWP view
All previous sign-offs are stored in a Sign-Off History section (viewable as a log/timeline)
E-signature support: clicking Sign Off records the user's digital signature (name + role + timestamp) as a formal sign-off entry — NO drawing pad required
Open AWPs must appear as a panel on the main Dashboard with their current approval status visible at a glance.
The MOV table must be structured as follows:
Document name + Auditor's Google Drive link for each required document
Secondary auditee response or document status dropdown
Tertiary auditee response or remarks dropdown
Each row has an Add Row (+) button to allow auditors to add more documents
Auditors list every document they need, with a direct Google Drive link per item
Auditees respond using dropdown selections in Columns 2, 3, and 4
A visual progress bar or indicator must be displayed per engagement showing the percentage of MOVs that have been submitted/completed. This must be visible on the main Dashboard.
A dedicated MOV Dashboard view must:
Read and aggregate all MOV inputs from auditors and auditees
Allow filtering by auditor, document type, or status
A separate Inventory of MOVs section must provide a complete catalog of all MOV documents submitted across all engagements, with filters and search functionality.
The system must support the generation of audit tools for each engagement. Requirements:
Tools are NOT auto-generated — they are created by clicking a designated button inside an engagement
Each generated tool is clickable and opens to a sub-page where files can be uploaded and data can be entered
Generated tools are listed in the Generated All Tools panel on the Dashboard
The following tools must be available for generation within an engagement:
Other tools as needed (with + Add capability)
A dedicated module for IAS Cares content. Full specifications to be defined in a follow-up session with stakeholders. The module must have a dedicated entry on the Dashboard.
AAPES must have its own sub-dashboard showing relevant data and status. Full specifications to be confirmed. Must be integrated into the main Dashboard as a panel.
A compliance management module accessible from the dashboard. Must include tracking of compliance-related findings and follow-up actions.
Covers the complete planning phase of an audit engagement. Includes pre-audit activities, resource allocation, and scheduling. Full specifications to be provided.
The following items require confirmation before development begins:
What exactly should the IAS Cares module contain? What data does it track?
What exactly should AAPES contain and display on its dashboard?
What does 'Buong Planning' include specifically? What forms and fields?
For MOV Columns 2-4 dropdowns — what are the specific dropdown options for Auditees?
Should the Flowchart be a file upload only, or should there be a built-in flowchart builder?
Should strict role restrictions apply for AWP sign-off? (e.g., only Director role can click Approve as Director)
For the Gov Mail login — should the system support SSO with the government mail provider, or just accept .gov.ph emails as valid addresses?
What specific notifications should be sent and to whom when an AWP is opened?
Should the Audit Feedback Survey Form be a fillable form inside the system, or just a file upload?
